title: How scientists tell the age of rocks
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: How do we know how old rocks are?

explain.say: When a rock crystal forms, it traps a few radioactive atoms, like uranium. These atoms slowly and steadily change, or decay, into other atoms, like lead, at a rate that never changes.

draw.text: How scientists tell the age of rocks

explain.say: The time for half of the radioactive atoms to decay is called the half-life. After one half-life, half are left; after two, a quarter; after three, an eighth.
By measuring how many original atoms are left compared to the new ones, scientists can work out how many half-lives have passed, like reading a clock built into the rock.
Uranium-238 has a half-life of about 4.5 billion years, perfect for very old rocks. Dating meteorites and the oldest rocks this way shows the Earth is about 4.54 billion years old.

faq.a: A half-life is the time it takes for half of the radioactive atoms in a sample to decay. It is always the same for a given kind of atom, which makes it a reliable clock.

faq.q: How do we know how old rocks are?
faq.a: Scientists measure radioactive atoms in the rock and the atoms they decay into. Because the decay rate is fixed, the ratio tells how long ago the crystal formed. This is called radiometric dating.
About 4.54 billion years old, found by radiometric dating of meteorites and the oldest Earth minerals.

faq.q: Can carbon dating tell the age of dinosaurs?
faq.a: No. Carbon-14 has a half-life of only about 5,730 years, so it works for things up to about 50,000 years old. Dinosaur ages come from dating volcanic rock layers with longer-lived atoms, like uranium or potassium.
asks: Is carbon dating used for rocks?

faq.q: What is the oldest rock or mineral found?
faq.a: Tiny zircon crystals from Jack Hills in Western Australia are about 4.4 billion years old, the oldest known pieces of Earth.

facts: Uranium-238 has a half-life of about 4.47 billion years.
Carbon-14 has a half-life of about 5,730 years.
Zircon crystals from the Jack Hills in Western Australia are about 4.4 billion years old.

quiz.say: A rock has one quarter of its original radioactive atoms left. How many half-lives have passed?
quiz.why: After one half-life half is left, and after two, half of a half, which is one quarter.

wrong.1: After one half-life, one half would be left.
wrong.2: After four half-lives, only one sixteenth would be left.
